title: Scrolls - Develop and deploy Custom GraphQL chain indexes

ms.promise:
Integrate Deno / WASM runtime into Scrolls pipeline
Adapt processing logic for Map / Reduce operations
Adapt storage backend to accept custom schemas
ms.criteria: A new version of Scrolls that support custom indexing of custom schemas by enabling developers to plugin the map / reduce logic without having to deal with any of the common boilerplate.
ms.report:
Milestone Outputs:

・Integrate Deno / WASM runtime into Scrolls pipeline
・Successfully incorporated Deno / WASM runtime into the Scrolls pipeline, ensuring seamless compatibility and efficient execution.
・Adapt processing logic for Map / Reduce operations
・Implemented modifications in the processing logic to facilitate Map / Reduce operations, enhancing the versatility of data processing within Scrolls.
・Adapt storage backend to accept custom schemas
・Successfully adjusted the storage backend to accommodate custom schemas, providing developers the flexibility to define and use their own data structures.

Acceptance Criteria:

The success of Milestone 1 is determined by the following criteria:
・New Version of Scrolls: A new version of Scrolls has been developed and released, capable of supporting custom indexing for custom schemas.
・Plug-and-Play Map / Reduce Logic: Developers can seamlessly integrate their own Map / Reduce logic without dealing with common boilerplate code, simplifying the development process.

ms.promise:
Implement GraphQL server to serve custom schemas
Create end-to-end examples
ms.criteria: A flexible mechanism to query custom indexes using a well-known and popular mechanism (GraphQL)
ms.report:
Implement GraphQL server to serve custom schemas
Create end-to-end examples

We have created a example of a GraphQL server that serves custom schema 
https://github.com/txpipe/asteria/blob/523823b198b56a5960bfe6ff790c68546056bd57/backend/src/main.rs#L128
In this example it serves as a backend for UTxO based game called Project Asteria
The data comes from onchain actions indexed via Oura 
https://github.com/txpipe/oura/blob/67cc38151cc06014d52b6a73cbf74ae659c28ef4/examples/postgresql/daemon.toml
We then project raw UTxO CBOR into meaningful postgres schema / tables, like the position of the objects within the game using Mumak Postgres Extension 
https://github.com/txpipe/mumak/
With that we are able to do amazing capabilities like allowing via GraphQL doing a search algorithm (using Mahan Distance to detect objects within a certain radius for example)

Evidence of milestone completion 
Publicly available source code under Apache license of a GraphQL server that allows access to custom indexes defined in Scrolls.
https://github.com/txpipe/asteria/tree/main/backend
